speaker: Doctor
text: When did you first notice these symptoms, and have they been getting progressively worse over time? Do you have a history of high blood pressure or diabetes?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of head trauma, seizures, or any recent infections? Have you noticed any changes in your speech or vision recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any headaches, nausea, or vomiting, and do you have a history of cancer or blood clotting disorders? I will now request imaging to investigate potential structural causes. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years. Social history: Information not provided

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of untreated HIV, we need to urgently rule out opportunistic infections like Toxoplasmosis or Primary CNS Lymphoma causing these focal neurological deficits. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain with contrast: Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings are consistent with Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), a demyelinating disease caused by the JC virus in immunocompromised patients. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
